references.text: Nadab and Abihu took their fire pans, put fire in them, added incense to the fire, and this resulted in their death. This shows the dangers of approaching the Lord with unauthorized incense.
Aaron used a fire pan with incense on the Day of Atonement, illustrating the proper use of incense pans in worship.
Moses instructed Korah and his followers to take fire pans, which is the background for this action in verse 18.
The result of this action: fire came out from the Lord and consumed the 250 men who were offering incense.
The fire pans of those who were consumed were beaten into plates for the altar as a warning sign, showing the consequence of the event in 16:18.
The regulations concerning the incense offering that only Aaron and his sons were to perform, which Korah's group broke by offering incense.
The entrance to the tent of meeting was where the Lord met with His people, explaining why they stood there.
Incense in golden pans used before God's throne, illustrating the symbolic meaning of incense pans in worship.
